layers.note: A low shrub scattered among the bursage on gravelly slopes and mesas.

moisture.note: Dry gravelly slopes, mesas and the banks of washes.

elevation_m.note: Up to about 1,520 m (Kearney and Peebles: 5,000 feet or lower).

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 4 to 18 °C; gone below 1 °C and above 22 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −13 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −18 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 25 to 34 °C; gone below 22 °C, where summers are too short, and above 37 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 4,500 to 10,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 3,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 3,000 to 8,500 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 2,000.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.08, gone by 0.04.

summer_rain.note: Needs the summer monsoon: from about 0.25 of the year's precipitation falling in the July to September storms, gone below 0.1, where winter rain falls alone; the bajada gets about half its rain then. Up to about 0.85, gone by 0.9.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m) from general knowledge of the species, the ranges and elevations in Kearney and Peebles (1942) and, where one exists, the FEIS species review. Fairy duster grows from southeastern California through southern Arizona and New Mexico to western Texas and northern Mexico, in the Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts and desert grassland (Kearney and Peebles 1942; Abrams 1944). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
